properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-18, on proofs built from logical operators and their graph forms: "Logic Circuit Diagrams (Directed Acyclic Graphs) … Binary Decision Diagrams (BDDs) … Reduced Ordered BDDs … a complex logical formula is compressed into a canonical graph form … Logic Networks / And-Inverter Graphs … I feel that, for instance, a philosophical (used in a line of reasoning) 'and' is equivalent to the logical operator AND. So philosophy can take on true logical operations in their proofs".

WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY IS: a step's rule `all` is AND, `any` is OR, and `k_of_n` is a threshold gate, over holds/fails/unknown (Kleene's three-valued logic). A line of reasoning is therefore an AND/OR/threshold DAG, the same shape as a logic circuit. A conclusion's support is a Boolean function of its premises.

THE IDEA: compute, deterministically (reflow2's side of the agent/reflow2 line, dec:idea-what-reflow2-can-learn-from-evaluator-guided-llm-circuit-design and @ajs 2026-10-17), the MINIMAL CUT SETS of a conclusion. These are the smallest sets of premises whose joint rejection makes it unsupported, like a fault tree's minimal cut sets (a systems engineer's familiar tool). Or, equivalently, a reduced ordered BDD of its support function. It answers "reject these, and what falls, what survives?" for SETS of premises, through every step, not one premise one hop at a time. That is exactly the stated purpose of the Erikson argument (req:argument-is-the-deliverable in design 7aa8a90d21c8956c). The 2026-10-18 proof of concept found that today's what-if does not carry a failure past one hop.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- THE OPERATOR MATCHES; THE STRENGTH DOES NOT ALWAYS. A mathematical AND is entailment. A philosophical argument's "and" is often DEFEASIBLE (inference to the best explanation), where support is a matter of degree or standard, not all-or-nothing. Cut sets over all/any read every step as strict. That is why the kept idea "a proof standard per claim" (dec:idea-what-reflow2-takes-from-the-argumentation-frameworks, (d)) matters next to this.
- SIZE: minimal cut sets can be exponential in the worst case. For the designs seen (tens of premises) they are cheap, but a bound and a "capped" report are needed.
- OBJECTIONS: an opposing CONTRADICTS acts like a NOT on support. Cut sets should say whether they include "an objection becomes established" as a way to sink a claim.
- FEWER THINGS: one new read (a report), no new node type.
- A BDD as a VIEW is the agent's to draw (flo2 dec:idea-flo2-io-draws-a-proof-or-line-of-reasoning-as-a-graph, kept (b)/(c)). Computing the sets is reflow2's.

SIZE, as a finding: small to medium. It is a read over the existing support walk, and it depends on the walk carrying failure past one hop.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 compute a conclusion's minimal cut sets: which sets of premises, if rejected together, sink it (as a fault tree's minimal cut sets, or a reduced binary decision diagram of its support)?
